register: Neutral-formal; the standard verb for subjecting an activity, market or system to public rules or oversight.
trap: Portuguese regulamentar and French réglementer may prompt reglamentar; in Spanish, regular is the unmarked verb, while reglamentar stresses detailed implementing rules.
example_tl: La Unión Europea pretende regular los sistemas de recomendación sin imponer un modelo editorial único a todas las plataformas del continente.
example_en: The European Union intends to regulate recommendation systems without imposing a single editorial model on every platform on the continent.
cloze: La Unión Europea pretende {{c1::regular}} los sistemas de recomendación sin imponer un modelo editorial único a todas las plataformas del continente.
note: The legacy rendering is correct; the teaching value lies in resisting cross-language pressure toward the narrower reglamentar.

register: Critical social-science and media vocabulary; marks the transformation of something into a tradable good, often with a negative evaluation.
trap: Comercializar means to market or sell something; it does not by itself express turning a social good, relationship or activity into a commodity.
example_tl: Las plataformas han mercantilizado la atención pública hasta convertir cada pausa, conversación y desplazamiento en una oportunidad de extracción de datos.
example_en: Platforms have commodified public attention to the point of turning every pause, conversation and journey into an opportunity for data extraction.
cloze: Las plataformas han {{c1::mercantilizado}} la atención pública hasta convertir cada pausa, conversación y desplazamiento en una oportunidad de extracción de datos.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate for the intended critical sense.

register: Neutral; vigilar covers systematic observation by state or private actors, while someter a vigilancia is more explicitly institutional.
trap: French surveiller and Italian sorvegliare do not license a Spanish cognate such as *surveillar; supervisar means oversee, not secretly or systematically monitor.
example_tl: Durante años, las autoridades vigilaron a activistas y periodistas mediante herramientas adquiridas oficialmente para investigar delitos graves y proteger la seguridad nacional.
example_en: For years, the authorities surveilled activists and journalists using tools officially acquired to investigate serious crimes and protect national security.
cloze: Durante años, las autoridades {{c1::vigilaron}} a activistas y periodistas mediante herramientas adquiridas oficialmente para investigar delitos graves y proteger la seguridad nacional.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Self-review: replaced the ambiguous provider with public authorities, making the agent and the acquisition of surveillance tools coherent.

register: Neutral in economic and public-policy writing; context determines whether the transfer is presented descriptively or critically.
trap: The infinitival to is not a purpose phrase here: translating it as para produces the malformed headword para privatizar found in the legacy gloss.
example_tl: El Gobierno privatizó la infraestructura de pagos sin establecer salvaguardias que impidieran que el nuevo operador excluyera a competidores y encareciera el servicio.
example_en: The government privatized the payment infrastructure without establishing safeguards to prevent the new operator from excluding competitors and making the service more expensive.
cloze: El Gobierno {{c1::privatizó}} la infraestructura de pagos sin establecer salvaguardias que impidieran que el nuevo operador excluyera a competidores y encareciera el servicio.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which mistakes the English infinitive marker for the Spanish purpose preposition para. Self-review: replaced the compressed impedir a alguien + infinitive construction with a finite subordinate clause for more idiomatic policy prose.

register: Neutral-critical for a lasting disturbance or radical alteration; avoids the promotional tone that revolucionar often carries in technology discourse.
trap: Interrumpir means stopping an ongoing process or service; it is too narrow when disrupt means profoundly altering an industry, institution or social system.
example_tl: La entrada de fondos especulativos trastocó el ecosistema mediático local, debilitó las redacciones y subordinó la cobertura a métricas de rentabilidad inmediata.
example_en: The arrival of speculative funds disrupted the local media ecosystem, weakened newsrooms and subordinated coverage to metrics of immediate profitability.
cloze: La entrada de fondos especulativos {{c1::trastocó}} el ecosistema mediático local, debilitó las redacciones y subordinó la cobertura a métricas de rentabilidad inmediata.
note: The isolated English prompt is polysemous. This note adopts the lasting industry-change sense supported by the topic; old_back remains valid for interrupting an event or service.

register: Written-formal; standard in political theory and criticism for durable dominance sustained through institutions, norms or consent.
trap: Spanish writes hegemonía: Italian egemonia may prompt loss of the initial h, while French hégémonie may prompt a spurious accent on e instead of the required í.
example_tl: La hegemonía de dos plataformas sobre la publicidad digital condiciona qué medios sobreviven y limita el pluralismo sin necesidad de censura explícita.
example_en: The hegemony of two platforms over digital advertising determines which media outlets survive and limits pluralism without requiring explicit censorship.
cloze: {{c1::La hegemonía}} de dos plataformas sobre la publicidad digital condiciona qué medios sobreviven y limita el pluralismo sin necesidad de censura explícita.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from unnecessary capitalization. Independent audit: separated the Italian h-loss risk from the French accent-placement risk.

register: Neutral-formal political term, often evaluatively negative when power is concentrated in a small economic or technological elite.
trap: Italian oligarchia and French oligarchie can obscure the Spanish spelling: oligarquía is feminine and requires qu before í plus a written accent.
example_tl: La oligarquía tecnológica no necesita ocupar ministerios: le basta con financiar laboratorios, influir en los estándares y contratar a quienes redactaron las normas.
example_en: The technological oligarchy does not need to occupy ministries: it need only fund laboratories, shape standards and hire those who drafted the rules.
cloze: {{c1::La oligarquía}} tecnológica no necesita ocupar ministerios: le basta con financiar laboratorios, influir en los estándares y contratar a quienes redactaron las normas.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review: replaced the calqued condicionar estándares with the idiomatic influir en los estándares and restored con after bastar.

register: Neutral academic and argumentative vocabulary for an apparently contradictory result or proposition.
trap: Spanish paradoja is feminine and ends in -ja; Portuguese o paradoxo, Italian il paradosso, French le paradoxe and German das Paradox all invite gender or spelling transfer.
example_tl: La paradoja de la moderación automática es que elimina el contexto precisamente cuando pretende aplicar las reglas con mayor coherencia y neutralidad.
example_en: The paradox of automated moderation is that it removes context precisely when it seeks to apply the rules with greater consistency and neutrality.
cloze: {{c1::La paradoja}} de la moderación automática es que elimina el contexto precisamente cuando pretende aplicar las reglas con mayor coherencia y neutralidad.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from unnecessary capitalization; the card retains the item for its cross-language gender and spelling trap. Self-review: added the article in elimina el contexto to remove English-influenced article omission. Independent audit: distinguished gender transfer from spelling transfer across the learner's four other languages.

register: Neutral-formal in constitutional, geopolitical and technology-policy writing; often specified by a domain such as digital or technological sovereignty.
trap: Use soberanía, not *soberanidad; the feminine noun carries a written accent on í and differs visibly from Italian sovranità.
example_tl: La soberanía tecnológica exige capacidad pública para auditar infraestructuras críticas, no una imposible autosuficiencia nacional en cada eslabón de la cadena de suministro digital.
example_en: Technological sovereignty requires public capacity to audit critical infrastructure, not impossible national self-sufficiency at every link in the digital supply chain.
cloze: {{c1::La soberanía}} tecnológica exige capacidad pública para auditar infraestructuras críticas, no una imposible autosuficiencia nacional en cada eslabón de la cadena de suministro digital.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review: replaced the vague componente de la cadena digital with the established supply-chain phrasing eslabón de la cadena de suministro digital.

register: Neutral-formal academic term for an organizing model or conceptual framework; frequent but often overused in institutional prose.
trap: Paradigma is masculine despite its final -a, so use el or un, not *la or *una.
example_tl: El paradigma tecnológico basado en la publicidad convirtió la extracción masiva de datos en condición tácita para acceder a servicios aparentemente gratuitos.
example_en: The advertising-based technological paradigm turned mass data extraction into an implicit condition for accessing apparently free services.
cloze: {{c1::El paradigma}} tecnológico basado en la publicidad convirtió la extracción masiva de datos en condición tácita para acceder a servicios aparentemente gratuitos.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from unnecessary capitalization. Independent audit: replaced the strained paradigma de innovación financiado con publicidad with paradigma tecnológico basado en la publicidad; the masculine modifiers still reinforce the headword's gender.

register: Formal technical and regulatory usage for correspondence with a rule or standard; social conformity may instead require conformismo or conformidad social.
trap: Conformismo denotes passive acceptance of prevailing attitudes, not technical conformity with a standard; the legacy gloss therefore narrows the English incorrectly.
example_tl: La auditoría certificó la conformidad con las normas europeas, pero omitió evaluar si el algoritmo discriminaba indirectamente a los solicitantes extranjeros.
example_en: The audit certified conformity with European standards but failed to assess whether the algorithm indirectly discriminated against foreign applicants.
cloze: La auditoría certificó {{c1::la conformidad}} {{c1::con}} las normas europeas, pero omitió evaluar si el algoritmo discriminaba indirectamente a los solicitantes extranjeros.
note: Materially diverges from old_back. The source is underspecified; the note teaches the regulatory sense, while conformismo remains possible only for social or behavioral conformity.

register: Neutral-critical for technology or monitoring that encroaches on privacy; invasivo is standard in medical and ecological contexts and also occurs more broadly.
trap: English invasive and Italian invasivo can make invasivo automatic; in privacy contexts, intrusivo often identifies the unwanted intrusion more precisely.
example_tl: El regulador prohibió un sistema intrusivo de verificación de edad que obligaba a todos los usuarios a ceder datos biométricos.
example_en: The regulator banned an invasive age-verification system that required all users to hand over biometric data.
cloze: El regulador prohibió un sistema {{c1::intrusivo}} de verificación de edad que obligaba a todos los usuarios a ceder datos biométricos.
note: The isolated source is underspecified. Old_back is valid generally; intrusivo is selected for the privacy-encroachment sense fixed by the example. Self-review: replaced documentos biométricos with datos biométricos to name the privacy-sensitive material precisely.

register: Written-formal; aseveración presents a proposition as stated confidently, while afirmación is the more neutral and frequent alternative.
example_tl: La aseveración de que el algoritmo es neutral carece de respaldo empírico y oculta decisiones normativas adoptadas por sus diseñadores.
example_en: The assertion that the algorithm is neutral lacks empirical support and conceals normative decisions made by its designers.
cloze: {{c1::La aseveración}} de que el algoritmo es neutral carece de respaldo empírico y oculta decisiones normativas adoptadas por sus diseñadores.
note: The legacy afirmación is valid and remains an alternative; aseveración better fixes the confident argumentative sense demonstrated here. Self-review: removed an overstated warning about aserción, which is a valid general synonym, so no genuine trap remains.

register: Written-formal argumentative sense: a proposition advanced and defended in debate, not a dispute or an act of restraint.
trap: Contención means containment, restraint or cost control; it is a false friend for contention when the English noun means an argumentative claim.
example_tl: La tesis de que la autorregulación basta para proteger el pluralismo ignora los incentivos comerciales que premian la polarización y el contenido extremo.
example_en: The contention that self-regulation is enough to protect pluralism ignores the commercial incentives that reward polarization and extreme content.
cloze: {{c1::La tesis}} de que la autorregulación basta para proteger el pluralismo ignora los incentivos comerciales que premian la polarización y el contenido extremo.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which selects the unrelated containment sense; the argumentative reading is also confirmed by the canonical Italian rebuild note.
